## Your commands

### gov work

start or continue a project, and open your agent in it

```text
gov work [<project-id>] [--project <pattern>] [--agent <id>] [--seed] [--print-prompt]
```

**Where.** anywhere. Inside a project, it continues THAT project

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<project-id>` | a project to open, e.g. PRJ-43-billing. Without one, gov asks |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--project <pattern>` | match a project by a regular expression instead of picking from a list |
| `--agent <id>` | the agent to launch (`gov agent list` shows what your org approves) |
| `--seed` | allow STARTING a project nobody has started yet — org-visible, so never implied |
| `--print-prompt` | print the session-start prompt and stop: changes nothing, launches nothing |

**Examples**

```bash
gov work
gov work --project=billing
gov work --project=PRJ-43-billing --agent=claude --print-prompt
```

**Changes.** clones the project's repos if they are not here, puts each on the project branch, writes the agent harness and the governance snapshot into the project folder, and launches your agent

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo; you have no write access to the project's board |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov seed](#gov-seed) · [gov join](#gov-join) · [gov agent](#gov-agent) · [gov preferences](#gov-preferences)

### gov org

the governance workspaces on this machine, and which one is active

```text
gov org <add|use|list|remove> [<github_org>] [--home <path>]
```

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<github_org>` | the organization, as GitHub spells it |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <path>` | where that org's governance repo is cloned (for `add`) |

**Examples**

```bash
gov org list
gov org use acme
gov org add acme --home ~/.gov/acme/gov_repo
```

**Changes.** writes the machine's registry (~/.gov/workspaces and ~/.gov/active). Touches no repository

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov setup](#gov-setup) · [gov doctor](#gov-doctor)

### gov doctor

check this machine: git, gh, the workspace, the active org, versions

```text
gov doctor [--fix] [--gov-home <path>]
```

**Where.** anywhere — it is the command for a machine that is not set up yet

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--fix` | offer to install or configure what is missing, one step at a time, asking first |
| `--gov-home <path>` | check a workspace other than the active one |

**Examples**

```bash
gov doctor
gov doctor --fix
```

**Changes.** nothing, unless `--fix` is given and you agree to a step; then it installs tools or writes git config

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | ready, or ready once you follow the notes |
| `1` | something is missing that gov cannot work without |

**See also.** [gov setup](#gov-setup) · [gov org](#gov-org) · [gov upgrade](#gov-upgrade)

### gov setup

set this machine up for an organization — the first `gov` run does this for you

```text
gov setup [<github_org>/<repo>] [--non-interactive] [--path <dir>]
```

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<github_org>/<repo>` | create a NEW governance repo for that org. Without it, configure the workspace you are in |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--non-interactive` | never create anything and never ask; for CI |
| `--path <dir>` | where to put the clone |

**Examples**

```bash
gov setup
gov setup acme/acme-gov
```

**Changes.** with an argument: creates the org's governance repository on GitHub, clones it, seeds the framework content, registers and activates it. Without one: configures the workspace you are standing in

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov org](#gov-org) · [gov doctor](#gov-doctor)

### gov upgrade

pull the latest framework content into this org (not the CLI — that is `npm i -g`)

```text
gov upgrade [--apply] [--pr] [--ref <branch>] [--from <dir>]
```

**Where.** GOVERNED — the org's workspace

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--apply` | make the changes. Without it, gov only says what it would do |
| `--pr` | put the changes in a pull request instead of the working tree |
| `--ref <branch>` | take the content from another branch of the framework |
| `--from <dir>` | take the content from a local directory instead of the template remote |

**Examples**

```bash
gov upgrade
gov upgrade --pr
gov upgrade --apply
```

**Changes.** with `--apply`: rewrites framework-owned files, leaves the org's own alone, merges org-config key by key, and removes what the new layout retires. With `--pr`: the same, on a branch, as a pull request

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov doctor](#gov-doctor) · [gov validate](#gov-validate)

### gov log

what gov did — one log per run, on this machine

```text
gov log [<run-id>] [--last] [--project <name>] [--limit <n>]
```

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<run-id>` | the four characters a failure printed, e.g. 7f3a |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--last` | the newest run: its folder, then its lines |
| `--project <name>` | only runs about that project |
| `--limit <n>` | how many to list (default 20) |

**Examples**

```bash
gov log

```

**Changes.** nothing — it reads what earlier runs recorded

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | listed, or printed |
| `1` | no organization on this machine yet |

**See also.** [gov doctor](#gov-doctor) · [gov preferences](#gov-preferences)

### gov agent

which AI agents your org approves, what is installed, and how to add one

```text
gov agent [list | install <id> | approve <id>]
```

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |

**Examples**

```bash

```

**Changes.** `install` installs the vendor's tool on this machine (it shows the vendor's URL first and asks). `approve` opens a pull request against your org's agent policy — it does not decide it

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov work](#gov-work) · [gov preferences](#gov-preferences)

### gov rules

compile the policies into what agents and checks actually use

```text
gov rules <build|check|report|reload> [--working-tree]
```

**Where.** GOVERNED

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<mode>` | build (write) · check (verify, write nothing) · report (the numbers only) · reload (attest that you restarted your session, after the rules changed) |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--working-tree` | compile what is on disk instead of the ratified branch — for drafting; an agent is still governed by the default branch |

**Examples**

```bash
gov rules report
gov rules build
gov rules reload
```

**Changes.** `build` writes the nine agent instruction files, `agent/harness/rule-map.md` and the POL lock; `check` writes nothing and fails when any of them is stale; `report` writes nothing at all. A clause that cannot be numbered without a decision STOPS the build — nothing is written and the question is printed. `reload` clears the `rules-pending` marker that `gov sync`/`gov upgrade` left when the rules changed, and records in the run log that YOU attested to restarting your agent session — who, when, which rules hash. It is not a way to avoid restarting: a session that did not restart is still reading superseded rules, and the log now names whoever said it had

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | a notation error, a stale file, or a question only a person can answer |
| `2` | usage |

**See also.** [gov knowledge](#gov-knowledge) · [gov doctor](#gov-doctor) · [gov validate](#gov-validate)

## Your agent runs these (you can too)

### gov seed

start a project from a GitHub Project board

```text
gov seed <board-url> [--assignee <login>] [--clean [--consent]]
```

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<board-url>` | the board this project is run from |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--assignee <login>` | who the anchor issue is assigned to (default: you) |
| `--clean` | remove a half-finished earlier attempt first; needs --consent |

**Examples**

```bash
gov seed https://github.com/orgs/acme/projects/43
```

**Changes.** creates the project branch in the workspace and in every linked repo, pushes them, creates the anchor issue on the board and assigns it, and scaffolds projects/&lt;id&gt;/ with its knowledge files

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo; a half-finished attempt is in the way — `--clean --consent` clears it |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov work](#gov-work) · [gov join](#gov-join) · [gov close](#gov-close)

```bash
gov join https://github.com/orgs/acme/projects/43
gov join PRJ-43-billing
```

| code | means |

### gov task

start a task: a sub-branch for one or more issues, in every repo of the project

```text
gov task <issue-url>[,<issue-url>…]
```

**Where.** PROJECT — inside the project the issues belong to

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<issue-url>` | a GitHub issue on this project's board. Several, comma-separated, share one branch |

**Examples**

```bash
gov task https://github.com/acme/app/issues/42
gov task https://github.com/acme/app/issues/42,https://github.com/acme/app/issues/43
```

**Changes.** creates &lt;project-branch&gt;.ISSUE-&lt;n&gt; in the workspace and each code repo and pushes it; assigns the issues to you and moves them to In progress

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo; the issue is closed, or you are not authorized on the board — nothing was created |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov merge](#gov-merge) · [gov work](#gov-work)

### gov merge

land a task sub-branch back on the project branch

```text
gov merge <issue-url | task-branch>
```

**Where.** PROJECT

**Examples**

```bash
gov merge https://github.com/acme/app/issues/42
gov merge BRNCH-43-billing.ISSUE-42
```

**Changes.** merges the sub-branch into the project branch in every repo that has it, pushes, deletes the sub-branch, and closes the issue

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo; the test-merge gate failed, or a repo refused the push — nothing was landed |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov task](#gov-task) · [gov close](#gov-close)

### gov knowledge

search and read the org's knowledge — or propose a change to it

```text
gov knowledge search <text> [--json] | show <path> | list [<prefix>] | <propose|submit|archive> <slug>
```

**Where.** GOVERNED

**Arguments**

| argument | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<text>` | what you are looking for; every word must appear. "quote a phrase" to keep it together |
| `<path>` | a path search printed, its tail, or the file name alone |
| `<slug>` | a short kebab-case name for a change, e.g. deploy-policy |

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | the same answer as data — how an agent retrieves knowledge (no service, no network) |
| `--limit <n>` | how many results to show (default 20) |
| `--description <text>` | why the change matters (submit) |

**Examples**

```bash
gov knowledge search "data classification"
gov knowledge show framework-policy.md
gov knowledge list policies/
gov knowledge propose deploy-policy
```

**Changes.** `search`/`show`/`list` change nothing — they read the markdown already in your workspace (org knowledge, policies, framework docs and every project's knowledge). `propose` creates and pushes a knowledge branch; `submit` opens the pull request to whoever owns that area; `archive` retires a knowledge file on a branch

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov close](#gov-close) · [gov validate](#gov-validate)

### gov issue

create an issue — assigned to you, on the board

```text
gov issue [<org>/<repo>] --title <t> [--body <b>|--body-file <f>] [--board <n>]  |  --from <upstream-issue-url> [--board <n>]
```

**Flags**

| flag | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--title <t>` | the issue's title |
| `--body <b> · --body-file <f>` | its body, inline or from a file |
| `--from <url>` | mirror an upstream issue into this org |
| `--board <n>` | the board to add it to (default: the current project's) |

**Examples**

```bash
gov issue --title "the picker paginates unevenly"
gov issue --from https://github.com/other/repo/issues/9
```

**Changes.** creates the issue on GitHub, assigns it to you, and adds it to the board

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

| `0` | everything the validators check passed |
| `1` | at least one validator failed; each is named |

**See also.** [gov doctor](#gov-doctor) · [gov knowledge](#gov-knowledge)

---

## Building gov itself

### gov bump-version

bump the CLI and content version together

```text
gov bump-version <x.y.z>
```

**Examples**

```bash
gov bump-version 1.3.0
```

**Changes.** writes publish/actions/ts/package.json and publish/content/VERSION in the framework repo

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | done |
| `1` | failed — nothing half-applied that gov could undo |
| `2` | usage: a missing or wrong argument |

**See also.** [gov publish](#gov-publish)

### gov publish

the pre-publish gate — never publishes by hand

```text
gov publish
```

**Examples**

```bash
gov publish
```

**Changes.** nothing: it runs the readiness gate (version-sync) and reports. Publishing is gov-cicd's

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | ready to publish |
| `1` | a blocker; each is named |

**See also.** [gov bump-version](#gov-bump-version) · [gov validate](#gov-validate)

### gov deps

retired — `gov doctor` reports the same prerequisites

```text
gov deps
```

**Examples**

```bash
gov doctor
```

**Changes.** nothing

**Exit codes**

| code | means |
| --- | --- |
| `2` | it says where it went |

**See also.** [gov doctor](#gov-doctor)

## Concepts

The ideas the commands assume. Short on purpose: a concept that needs a page of prose is a sign the
commands are wrong, not that the concept is deep.

### Projects and branches

A project is a GitHub Project board. GitHub is the source of truth: open board = active project.

```text
the board          github.com/orgs/<org>/projects/<n>
the project id     PRJ-<board#>-<slug>
the branch         BRNCH-<board#>-<slug>, in the workspace AND in every code repo
on your machine    <agent_work_root>/PRJ-<board#>-<slug>/
```

`gov seed` starts one, `gov join` brings someone else's to this machine, `gov work` opens it.
Its knowledge lives in projects/&lt;id&gt;/knowledge/ in the workspace repo.

### Tasks

A task is a sub-branch for one or more issues: &lt;project-branch&gt;.ISSUE-&lt;n&gt;, in every repo of the project.

```text
gov task <issue-url>      start it (creates and pushes the sub-branch, assigns the issues)
gov merge <issue-url>     land it (merges, pushes, deletes the sub-branch, closes the issue)
```

Several issues can share one task: pass them comma-separated. Task state is the issue's state on GitHub;
gov never keeps its own copy of it.

### Organizations and workspaces

A workspace is one organization's governance repository, cloned on this machine.

```text
~/.gov/workspaces         which orgs this machine knows, and where each is cloned
~/.gov/active             which one commands act on
<workspace>/org-config.yaml   the org's own values; every framework file reads them
```

`gov org list` shows them, `gov org use <org>` switches, `gov setup` adds the first one.
A machine may hold several; only one is active at a time.

### Context: PROJECT, GOVERNED, NONE

gov behaves differently depending on where you are standing, and says so in its banner.

```text
PROJECT    inside a project folder — work continues THAT project; task, merge, close apply to it
GOVERNED   in the org's workspace — org-wide commands (upgrade, knowledge, manage)
NONE       no workspace resolved — setup, org and doctor still work; they are how you leave NONE
```

If the banner says NONE unexpectedly, `gov doctor` says which of the three reasons it is.

### Preferences, credentials and state

Everything of yours lives in one folder: &lt;agent_work_root&gt;/preferences/&lt;your-gh-login&gt;/

```text
<login>.md          what your AGENT should take into account (prose, yours to write)
preferences.json    what the gov CLI needs: default agent, picker, colour, log retention
credentials         your agent API keys (0600) — gov loads them for the sessions it starts
state/              gov's own: the runs it logged, what you confirmed. Safe to delete
```

`gov preferences` lists every setting with its value and what it does. A preference chooses INSIDE what
your organization allows: a default agent your org has not approved is ignored, and gov says so.
